summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, prior diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and recent allogeneic stem cell transplant for EBV-positive Hodgkin lymphoma was admitted for fever, cough, and cavitary lung lesions on CT. She was evaluated for possible fungal or mycobacterial infection due to her immunocompromised state and prior TB exposure. Bronchoscopy with BAL revealed Staphylococcus aureus, with no evidence of TB, fungus, or viral pathogens. She was treated with a short course of levofloxacin and discharged home. Her graft-versus-host disease was managed with a prednisone taper and continued immunosuppression. She remained stable with no signs of lymphoma recurrence.
